reason: Attacked and it held. I read the Mooyaart-Doubleday text itself, not a quotation site: the Internet Archive full text of THE DIARY OF A YOUNG GIRL at in.ernet.dli.2015.201940, whose title page credits B. M. Mooyaart-Doubleday and which heads the entry 'Saturday, 15 July, 1944'. The passage there reads, character for character, 'It's really a wonder that I haven't dropped all my ideals, because they seem so absurd and impossible to carry out. Yet I keep them, because in spite of everything I still believe that people are really good at heart.' The absence of a comma after 'everything' is confirmed at the page, which matters because the form circulating on Goodreads, PassItOn and most quote sites inserts one; that comma is an internet artefact, not Mooyaart. The Massotty 1995 reading ('Yet I cling to them because I still believe, in spite of everything, that people are truly good at heart') is a different sentence and is correctly kept out. Two weaknesses in the verifier's evidence, neither fatal: (1) the evidence claims the English Wikiquote page 'marks the really good at heart wording as the variant translation' and credits the renderings to their translators. It does not. I fetched it; it prints the variants without attributing either to Mooyaart or Massotty. That claim should be struck and replaced with the scan I read. (2) The scan is a Washington Square Press Reader's Enrichment printing of the Mooyaart translation, not a page of the 1952 Doubleday first printing, so the source line's '1952' is the date of the translation's first publication rather than of any page anyone has opened. That is what rule four asks for, so it stands. Mechanics all pass: source line 104 characters, leads with the name, no dash, curly quotes only, quotation ends in a full stop, tag Diary is the form of the work, nothing shipped, no near match, Anne Frank at one of three for the year and her other line is in month 1, so no month collision. One editorial observation for the owner, not a defect: the month-1 Anne Frank line is Massotty's Definitive Edition of 1995 and this one is Mooyaart's of 1952, so the year will carry the same diarist in two different translations. That is permitted but it is worth a deliberate decision.
